title: Policy as code: OPA, Conftest and infrastructure checks

videos.script: Most companies already have security rules. They live on a wiki page. Images come from our registry. Nothing runs as root. Every container has a memory limit. {{wiki}} The page is read once, in somebody's first week. After that, the rule holds on the days somebody remembers it. This lesson turns those rules into code. {{rego}} You write them in Rego, the language of Open Policy Agent, and conftest runs them over your files. The Dockerfile first. Your rule fails on it straight away, and the reason is worth a minute. {{dockerfile}} Then the Kubernetes manifests, and a hurried change that breaks three rules at once. {{manifests}} A rule that stops working still passes, so the rules get tests of their own. {{tests}} You compare your rules with the hundreds Trivy ships, and see where they agree. Then the rules go into the pipeline, as a stage. {{pipeline}} The cluster already checks one of them at its door. By the end you will know why checking it twice is right. {{twice}}
